---
title: "D4Science cloud environment"
---

## Registration

To use the D4Science cloud environment, first register at [iriscc.d4science.org](https://iriscc.d4science.org/home). Click on "Register" and fill in the required information. After submitting the registration form, you will receive a confirmation email. Follow the instructions in the email to activate your account.

## Accessing the environment

Once your account is activated, log in to the D4Science portal at [iriscc.d4science.org](https://iriscc.d4science.org/home). After logging in, you will be directed to the dashboard where you can access the project environment and notebooks. To launch a JupyterLab session, click on "JupyterLab Start" in the dashboard. This will open a JupyterLab interface where you can navigate to the notebooks and start working.

::: {.callout-important}
The Flooding Risk demonstrator software is not yet pre-installed on D4Science. Once inside JupyterLab, follow the [installation instructions](installation.qmd) to install the environment manually before running any notebooks.
:::

## Registering the Jupyter kernel

After installing the environment, register it as a kernel so JupyterLab can find it. Open a terminal in JupyterLab and run:

```bash
pixi run python -m ipykernel install --user --name flood-demo --display-name "Python (flood-demo)"
```

Refresh JupyterLab and select `Python (flood-demo)` as the kernel when opening a notebook.

::: {.callout-important}
For Solara widgets and maps to render correctly in the notebooks, the D4Science JupyterLab server requires the following packages to be installed in its server-side Python environment. If widgets fail to load in the notebooks, run the following commands in the terminal:

```bash
pixi run pip install "ipyvuetify==1.11.3"
pixi run pip install ipyleaflet
```

Then refresh the webpage / kernel, and try again
:::

Alternatively, you can also use the `pixi run` command to start JupyterLab with the correct environment and kernel already selected:

```bash
pixi run jupyter lab
```

`Pixi` environment also includes the function to start the Solara App of the model-builder notebooks directly in the correct environment, without the need to start JupyterLab first. You can run the following command in the terminal:

```bash
pixi run solara-sfincs
```

::: {.callout-tip}
If you see errors about missing extensions (e.g. `ipyvuetify` or `ipyvue`) after selecting the kernel, try this sequence:

1. Open the notebook and select the `Python (flood-demo)` kernel
2. Close the notebook
3. Reopen the notebook

The notebook will now start directly with the correct kernel and the extension errors should be gone.
:::
